brief.title: Should we replace markdown PDFs?
brief.context: Markdown exports are fast but bland. The current need is branded, reusable business PDFs without a large design toolchain.

signals.label: Quality
signals.note: Real layout, hierarchy, and print CSS.

signals.label: Ops burden
signals.note: Python script, JSON data, source-controlled templates.

signals.label: Risk
signals.note: CSS support and native dependencies must be verified.

risks: Pretty sample data hides overflow bugs
brief.recommendation: Use WeasyPrint for owned designed PDFs; keep Playwright for JS-heavy pages.
brief.rationale: It keeps the authoring model simple while producing substantially better PDFs than generic exports.
